source_images_viewed.observation: Physical p.1 was actually displayed: title, Daniel Hadas and Ron Peled, DOI 10.4171/JEMS/1680, JEMS 28 (2026), 5023-5106 and revised 14 November 2024 are legible. The frozen 2025 identity remains distinct from the print year.

Physical p.4: Figure 1.1 was actually displayed with the four fully packed row/column parity classes. Color conventions and periodic/extremal-measure definitions correspond to the report's exact scope.

Physical p.5: Figure 1.2 was actually displayed, comparing a fully packed configuration, independent one-dimensional columns and a two-dimensional high-fugacity sample. Panels and labels agree with the caption.

Physical p.12: Figure 1.3 was actually displayed. Green sticks, left vertical/right horizontal configurations and the distinction between R2 and R1/R3 at the interface match the explanatory Peierls discussion.

Physical p.19 / printed p.5041: Figure 2.1 was actually displayed. The green even-rectangle boundary, four parity-colored interior tiles, and the right-hand 0/1 vertex configuration match the caption and the boundary-condition definitions. The vacancy weight lambda^{-#vacant faces/4} in (2.3) is legible.

Physical p.24 / printed p.5046: Figure 3.1 was actually displayed. The red block R and its blue reflected images form the indicated representative set inside/over the green Lambda boundary; the reflected R glyphs and background parity colors match the caption. Proposition 3.3 and the reflection-positivity dependency are legible; imported reflection-positivity theorems were not independently reproved.

Physical p.30 / printed p.5052: Figure 4.1 was actually displayed. Green sticks, the nested black R1/S1 and R2/S2 rectangles, and the difference between separately divided rectangles and a common dividing stick match the caption and Lemma 4.1. No source/layout ambiguity was observed in this illustration.

Physical p.32 / printed p.5054: Proposition 4.4 explicitly assumes even L; Corollary 4.5's vacancy seminorm bound lambda^{-1/4} and occupied-face deficit bound are legible and match the existing P1 and P2 dependencies.

Physical p.33 / printed p.5055: Remark 4.7 defines the global Etilde_M event and states M>=1, M|L and the partition-function equality/lower bound without an even-M condition. The exact text and symbols match P2; the earlier correctly even-length proposition is retained as counterevidence.

Physical p.37 / printed p.5059: Figure 4.2 was actually displayed. Four colored tiles surround the central vacancy f; offset pink/yellow boundary paths cross near f. Lemma 4.11's two-cycle construction and caption correspond to the existing textual proof-chain check.

Physical p.38 / printed p.5060: The proof's second crossing distinct from f is legible. Figure 4.3 displays the three compressed marked components with (v_H,k_H)=(4,3),(8,5),(12,4); Corollary 4.12 and the 2(k_H-1) bound match the report.

Physical p.52 / printed p.5074: Lemma 6.7's block-change roots, local central-reflection invariance and the unconditioned periodic-Gibbs scope of (6.2)/(6.4) were visually checked against the existing conditioning finding.

Physical p.63 / printed p.5085: The finite block roots 9,15,3 and the order of fixed constants before the fugacity choice are visible. These pages belong to the earlier phase-classification chain, distinguished from P1.
Physical p.65 / printed p.5087: The sealed-rectangle/vacancy-pair confinement of disagreement components is legible and corresponds to the existing uniqueness-chain coverage.

Physical p.69 / printed p.5091: Theorem 9.1 proof specifies arbitrary Omega_tilde containing J before (9.2). Theta is all vertices outside J, while the paragraph after (9.3) drops J when asserting unconditional rarity under the conditioned measure. The exact target of P1 was visually confirmed.
Physical p.70 / printed p.5092: The uses of (9.3), (9.4), (9.2) and the quantitative correlation step in Lemma 9.2 are legible, matching P1's bounded impact claim.

Physical p.71 / printed p.5093: The partition by the smaller correlation estimate, Remark 9.4's predicted sharpness and Theorem 9.5's dependence on Theorem 9.1 are visible. No conjectural prediction was promoted to proof.

Physical p.76 / printed p.5098: Tables 1 and 2 were actually displayed with yellow highlights. Table 1 maps Z^2 k-NN indices to D^2 and highlights the listed first sliding cases; Table 2 highlights H2 cases D^2=4,7,31,133. Captions and highlighted cells are visible and consistent with the surrounding discussion. This is a visual correspondence check, not an independent proof of the imported ground-state classifications.

Physical p.77 / printed p.5099: Figure 10.1 was actually displayed. Two D^2=29 M-triangles share a sliding base in panel (i), and panel (ii) shows gray M-triangle portions of a triangulated configuration. The surrounding text explicitly presents a high-fugacity heuristic; visual correspondence was confirmed without treating it as a proved classification.

Physical p.78 / printed p.5100: Figure 10.2 was actually displayed: D^2=29, lambda=2000, torus 259 by 161, diagonal columns and triangulation. Its heuristic discussion is distinguished from rigorous results; no simulation was rerun.

Physical p.79 / printed p.5101: Figure 10.3's two H2, D^2=4, lambda=700 MCMC panels and differing initial states were actually viewed. The text explicitly notes nonconvergence; visual correspondence does not certify the simulation.

Physical p.80 / printed p.5102: Figure 10.4 was actually displayed. Colored hexagonal trimers for H2, D^2=7 and the lambda=600 MCMC sample are visible and consistent with the caption. Simulation/classification was not independently rerun or proved.
